title: An Ellingham diagram: when carbon reduces iron oxide
caption: ΔG° per mole of O₂ against temperature. Forming CO gets more favourable as T rises (its line slopes down, ΔS > 0), while forming FeO gets less favourable. Above the crossing, about 994 K, carbon's line is lower, so carbon can reduce FeO.
alt: Two lines of ΔG° against temperature: 2C + O₂ → 2CO falling, 2Fe + O₂ → 2FeO rising; they cross near 990 K.
description: They cross at about 994 K; above it carbon reduces FeO.

checks.name: at 1500 K the carbon line is lower: C can reduce FeO
